intro: School trials suggest peer-led efforts and bystander training can modestly reduce conflict and increase helping, and kindness tasks can raise peer acceptance. Well-being gains from kind acts in teens are small, uneven, and sometimes absent.

items.title: Changing climates of conflict: A social network experiment in 56 schools
items.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (via PubMed Central)
items.finding: Across 56 schools and 24,191 students, getting a small group of students to take a public stand against conflict cut disciplinary reports of conflict by an estimated 30%.

items.title: A Meta-Analysis of School-Based Bullying Prevention Programs' Effects on Bystander Intervention Behavior
items.publisher: School Psychology Review (abstract via Office of Justice Programs)
items.finding: Twelve school programs (12,874 students) modestly increased bystander intervention (g = .20), with larger effects in high school than earlier grades, but did not significantly raise empathy for victims.

items.title: The Effectiveness of the KiVa Bullying Prevention Program in Wales, UK: Results from a Pragmatic Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
items.finding: In 22 primary schools, a program built around changing bystander behavior did not produce a statistically significant effect on victimization, and the authors called for a larger trial with better implementation.

items.title: Kindness Counts: Prompting Prosocial Behavior in Preadolescents Boosts Peer Acceptance and Well-Being
items.finding: Students aged 9 to 11 who performed kind acts gained more peer acceptance than those who visited places, though both groups improved in well-being.

items.title: Evidence from a Randomized Controlled Trial that Altruism Moderates the Effect of Prosocial Acts on Adolescent Well-being
items.publisher: Journal of Youth and Adolescence (via PubMed Central)
items.finding: In a small trial of 97 teens, well-being trajectories did not differ across groups overall; benefits of kind acts appeared mainly in teens who scored high on altruism.

items.title: The efficacy of three types of gratitude interventions for promoting defending behavior in response to school bullying among Chinese early adolescents
items.finding: A gratitude curriculum and a gratitude journal raised early adolescents' gratitude and defending behavior relative to controls, while gratitude visits improved defending only compared with baseline.

items.title: The Association Between Prosocial Behavior and Mental Health: A Three-Level Meta-Analysis
items.finding: Across 366 effect sizes, prosocial behavior and mental health were positively correlated (r = 0.26) in samples concentrated among children, adolescents and young adults, with differences by study design.

limits: Many of these trials are small, short, or done in one country, and several found no overall effect. The sheet's specific moves (sitting with someone, a private message, a specific thank-you) are not tested one by one, and these findings do not mean teens should handle serious harm alone.
